articles.title: crossOriginIsolated is a tradeoff, not a checkbox - why my in-browser ML model runs single-threaded
articles.excerpt: crossOriginIsolated is a tradeoff, not a checkbox — why my in-browser ML model runs single-threaded If you run an ONNX model in the browser with onnxruntime-web, the multithreaded WASM build wants Sha…
articles.body: crossOriginIsolated is a tradeoff, not a checkbox — why my in-browser ML model runs single-threaded If you run an ONNX model in the browser with onnxruntime-web , the multithreaded WASM build wants SharedArrayBuffer . And SharedArrayBuffer is only available when the page is cross-origin isolated , which means you've shipped both a COOP and a COEP header. The tempting advice is "just enable cross-origin isolation." I want to show why we deliberately did not , in a real production app, and what the honest tradeoff looks like. What we actually do Our background-removal tool self-hosts a small model (u2netp) and runs it through onnxruntime-web 's wasm bundle. articles.body: Cursor is a code editor built on VS Code that adds an AI assistant directly into your workflow. You can chat with your codebase, ask it to explain code, generate a function, or help fix an error, all without switching to a browser tab. Why developers like it: the AI can see your open files and project context, so its answers are more specific than a generic chatbot. For beginners, this is useful for understanding unfamiliar code. You can select a function and ask what it does, or ask why a piece of code might fail. How to set it up well: Start with a small project, not your main production code. Learn the chat, inline edit, and autocomplete features on something you can break safely. Use Composer or chat for planning first.

articles.title: The Complete Guide to Technical Debt Tracking for Engineering Leaders
articles.excerpt: Every engineering team knows technical debt exists. Far fewer can tell you exactly where it lives, how much it costs, or whether it is growing. That gap between awareness and visibility is where techn…
articles.body: Every engineering team knows technical debt exists. Far fewer can tell you exactly where it lives, how much it costs, or whether it is growing. That gap between awareness and visibility is where technical debt tracking comes in. This guide covers what to track, how to measure it, which tools help, and how to build a practice that actually sticks. What is technical debt tracking Technical debt tracking is the practice of identifying, categorizing, and prioritizing code compromises, outdated dependencies, and architectural shortcuts in your codebase. Think of it like treating shortcuts as loans: you took them to move faster, but now you owe future work to pay them back. Tracking makes that loan visible, measurable, and systematically payable.

articles.title: Run security checks against your own MCP server in CI, and see the findings in GitHub
articles.excerpt: Most MCP security tooling reads a server's tool descriptions. That finds text that looks suspicious. It does not tell you what your server does when a client calls it. This post is about a small comma…
articles.body: Most MCP security tooling reads a server's tool descriptions . That finds text that looks suspicious. It does not tell you what your server does when a client calls it. This post is about a small command-line tool that does the second thing, for a server you run: it starts your server, connects as an MCP client, calls it, and reports what it observed. It is called protocolprobe-selftest , it is ISC-licensed, and the source is public: protocolprobe/protocolprobe-tools . I build ProtocolProbe , a directory of dated facts about the servers in the official MCP registry. This tool is the part that runs on your machine, not ours. We use it on nobody else's server: you point it at your own, and the results stay on your computer.

articles.body: What I Built What if an AI could help us preserve the memories we fear losing, without asking us to hand those memories over to someone else? That's the question behind GhostVault , an AI-powered digital memory archive that I'm planning to build using open-weight AI models and local inference. The idea came from the themes of Halloween and Día de los Muertos. Halloween makes us think about ghosts, forgotten places, and things that linger long after they've disappeared. Día de los Muertos reminds us that photographs, stories, traditions, and memories can keep the people we love close to us. I wanted to bring these two ideas together into something that is both a little spooky and genuinely meaningful.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 30, 1964: NASA's weird Lunar Landing Research Vehicle takes 1st test flight to help Apollo astronauts land on the moon
articles.excerpt: On October 30, 1964, NASA's Lunar Landing Research Vehicle, or LLRV, took to the skies for the first time. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On October 30, 1964, NASA's Lunar Landing Research Vehicle, or LLRV, took to the skies for the first time. The LLRV was a bizarre, four-legged flying contraption commonly known as the "Flying Bedstead." NASA used it to simulate moon landings and liftoffs on Earth to prepare for Apollo 11 , the first crewed lunar landing. The first person to give it a whirl was the X-15 pilot Joe Walker . During this test flight, he reached an altitude of about 10 feet, and he hovered there for about a minute. He did this two more times that same day. In all, he completed more than 30 test flights with the LLRV. These test flights took place at NASA's Dryden Flight Research Center in Edwards, California.

articles.title: Look up! China's mysterious space plane is visible over the US this week
articles.excerpt: Early risers across the U.S. could catch a glimpse of China's mysterious Shenlong spacecraft with the naked eye.
articles.body: China's secretive space plane is making a series of passes over the United States in the coming days and you could spot it with your own eyes! The mysterious spacecraft, Shenlong, is currently orbiting Earth on its fourth mission . Although we don't know what it's up to, China's space agency has said it is testing technologies that "will pave the way for more convenient and affordable round-trip methods for the peaceful use of space in the future." Under favorable conditions, Shenlong is bright enough to spot with the naked eye, according to Spaceweather.com. But you'll need to set your alarm early, as some of the best viewing opportunities are in the predawn sky. articles.title: Think Halloween is scary? This scorched alien world is a real-life cosmic horror story
articles.excerpt: Earth would be terrifying if we celebrated Halloween every 11 hours, a possibility on a super-Earth investigated by the JWST, if it wasn't so hellishly hot that no life could survive on its surface.
articles.body: Earth would be terrifying if we celebrated Halloween every 11 hours, a possibility on a super-Earth investigated by the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST). That is, if this extrasolar planet, or exoplanet, wasn't so hellishly hot that no life could survive on its surface. The exoplanet in question is the rocky lava planet TOI-561 b, located around 280 light-years away, which was discovered by NASA's exoplanet-hunting spacecraft TESS (Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite) in 2020. The planet is located so close to its star, TOI-561, that not only does it complete an orbit every 11 hours, but its surface temperatures reach in excess of 3,000 degrees Fahrenheit (1,800 degrees Celsius). That is so hot that astronomers once believed that TOI-561 b couldn't possibly possess an atmosphere.

articles.title: Patrick Stewart, renowned actor and ‘Star Trek’s’ Captain Picard, dies at 86
articles.excerpt: Patrick Stewart, the distinguished British actor of stage and screen, passed away Wednesday (Oct. 28) in Los Angeles at the age of 86.
articles.body: Less than a week after the fates took Walter Koenig from our galaxy, another " Star Trek " legend has left us: Sir Patrick Stewart has died at the age of 86. According to his spokesperson Kelly Bush Novak, the beloved Shakespearean actor passed away on Wednesday (Oct. 28) at his Los Angeles home after a short struggle with Alzheimer’s disease and Lewy body dementia. "He has been held in the warm embrace of family and friends, surrounded by live music, prayer, tears, laughter and the kind of profound emotion that only he could inspire after a lifetime of devotion to us all," Bush Novak shared.
